experiment: auxiliary identity classification head (variant B) — S1-ID vs S0-ID
verdict: FAIL — auxiliary head achieves perfect identity classification (1.000) but free-gen I2N does not improve beyond S1 baseline

geometry_S1-ID_vs_base.conclusion: S1-ID adapter geometry is identical to base model; merger LoRA barely moved visual embeddings

confusion_matrices_test.S1-ID: Most predictions are OTHER (model refuses to generate alias); occasional correct
confusion_matrices_test.S0-ID: Strong alias biases (Jora, Eris, Faro dominate); structured confusion, not random

visual_controls.conclusion: All visual attributes degraded vs base model (same for both S1-ID and S0-ID)

interpretation.key_finding: Auxiliary identity head achieves 100% accuracy — identity information is perfectly readable from LM hidden states at layer 1. Yet free-gen I2N remains at 0.267, far below the 0.90 gate.
causal_diagnosis: The model CAN represent identity (head reads it perfectly)
The model CANNOT use identity to drive alias generation
This is a readout/binding failure, not a representation failure
The alias CE loss does not benefit from the identity signal — the two objectives are decoupled
interpretation.S1_vs_S1-ID: S1-ID shows modest improvement in candidate ranking (0.533 vs 0.300) but free-gen remains broken. The model can recognize the correct alias when scored by log-prob, but cannot generate it.
interpretation.geometry_preserved: The merger LoRA training with aux loss did NOT alter visual embeddings — geometry is identical to base. The aux head learns from the existing identity structure without changing it.
interpretation.route_establishment: HALT — the image-to-alias binding cannot be established by any LoRA variant tested (S0, S1, S2, S3, S0-ID, S1-ID) with the current alias-CE training objective. The binding failure is robust to: scope changes, rank increases, auxiliary identity supervision, and capacity controls.
